Scope: phase 1 of the logistics area. Wet networks (sewerage, storm, potable water, fire fighting and TSE, including the force main), dry networks (medium voltage, low voltage, street lighting and telecom), the potable water pump station, the sewage lift station, guard rooms, all road layers up to the asphalt wearing course, and landscape.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 20-Oct-2026 data date the project is 57.9% complete against 71.1% planned, 13.2% behind the plan (SPI 0.81). It gained 2.1% this week against 5.5% planned, so the gap widened from 9.7% to 13.2%.

With 81.6% of the contract time gone, 42.1% of the work remains. Finishing by the contract completion date of 29-Jan-2027 needs about 2.9% a week, against 2.1% achieved this week. The revised plan reaches 92.9% by the end of November and 100% in December 2026. The weekly report's milestone sheet and the P6 update forecast project handover on 01-Mar-2027, 31 days late; the General Information sheet gives 14-Feb-2027. Construction is the weak phase: 45.1% done against 70.9% planned.

The P6 update finishes the project on 01-Mar-2027, 31 days after the contract completion date. The schedule has no finish constraint at the contract date, so its float is measured against its own late finish and no activity shows negative float. The asphalt wearing course has only 5 days of float and construction finish 12 days. The General Information sheet forecasts completion on 14-Feb-2027 and the look-ahead sheet on 30-Nov-2026, so the three forecasts in the report disagree.

Data notes

  • Report week: the weekly report states "Current Contract Weeks: 64 of 78" (Milestones sheet). The consultant's HSE and quality inspections use their own numbering (inspection No. 46, counted from 25-Nov-2025).
  • This report uses only the latest weekly report (data date 20-Oct-2026). Previous-week quantities are not in it, so the "This week" column of the quantities table shows "—"; the 13-Oct S-curve row is derived from this week's figures.
  • Three different completion forecasts: 14-Feb-2027 (General Information sheet, −16 days), 01-Mar-2027 (Milestones sheet and P6 update, −31 days) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet).
  • The P6 update has no finish constraint, so no activity shows negative float although it finishes after the contract date. 194 in-progress activities have finish dates before the data date.
  • Mobilisation: the weekly report gives 30-Aug-2025 as actual, the P6 milestone "Mobilization - Finish" gives 25-Nov-2025.
  • The "Complete earthworks" forecast of 25-Aug-2026 has passed but is still marked as a forecast, with earthworks at 96.2%. The "all materials delivered" forecast of 24-Oct-2026 conflicts with 58 of 155 materials not yet on site.
  • The procurement log cannot be used: delivered figures exceed quantities (for example 12,600 delivered of 2 MCCBs, 1,325,000 of 12 DI pipes), many cells show #DIV/0! or #VALUE!, and rows carry project ID DAM2-01-029. The front-page procurement total repeats the mechanical row (48 / 48 / 42) instead of 155 / 155 / 140, and shows 1 remaining PO against 15 implied.
  • NCRs: the front page shows 4 issued and 3 closed; the Quality-Stat sheet shows 51 issued and 49 closed.
  • Labour: the front page shows 360 planned and 483 actual; the Manpower sheet shows 78 planned and 537 actual for October, and its trade table plans 391.
  • Scope quantities in the Conclusion sheet differ from the Major Quantities sheet (sewer total 6,146 vs 7,567 LM, TSE total 17,678 vs 57,419 LM, telecom finished 1,000 vs 2,358 LM). Sewer pipes show 2.01 LM planned to date, and manholes and catch basins have fractional totals (for example 135.99).
  • Contract value is 198,906,162.61 on the front page and 198,906,162.312 "incl. VAT" in the Conclusion sheet. The invoice log has stray values (21,100,000, 20,900,000, 200,000) beside the contract values, and EAC shows #REF!.
  • Key submittal dates (quality, safety and baseline plans) are in Feb–Mar 2024, before the contract award of 30-Jun-2025. The look-ahead sheet contains P6 data from the Hail Industrial City Phase II project, and the risk register uses project ID DAM2-01-029 and names the 3rd and 6th Industrial Cities.
  • The action text of issue 1 still quotes 304 workers and 184 items of equipment, against 594 and 326 now on site.
  • Landscape shows 31.6% physical progress (ahead of its 19.7% plan) mostly from procurement credit; its construction part is only 1.0% done. The workbook's front page also reports cost-based progress as "earned"; this report uses physical progress only.
